headline: Latent generative models predict single-cell perturbation responses across modalities
label: Single Cell Generative Latent Modeling
summary: Flow-matching, Schrödinger bridge, and foundation-model approaches are now applied to perturbation prediction and multi-omics integration in single-cell data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned latent structure over single-cell measurements, used to model perturbation responses and cross-modal relationships. Several items frame perturbation prediction as transport in latent space. DRIFT separates cells into invariant and perturbation-responsive blocks and applies conditional flow matching to the responsive block. scEGFlow uses energy-guided conditional flow matching to steer predictions for unseen conditions, and PerturbBridge learns a perturbation-conditioned latent Schrödinger Bridge between unpaired control and target cells. SHERLOCK models perturbation effects as latent interventions for causal and combinatorial inference, while Pop-Corn predicts perturbation-induced composition shifts directly from Perturb-seq data. A second group addresses integration across modalities and species, including MoTRUST, AtlasOT, Crecerelle, Speciesformer, and EpiZoo, the last a 2.6B-parameter mixture-of-experts model pretrained on ~20.9M cells. The set is heterogeneous, so the perturbation-transport framing applies to only part of it.
